title: Uploading
purpose: The footage leaves every phone and reaches the client, complete and on time. This is the subsystem that lost the most in August.
how: One hour of footage is 5.4 GB. At 1,000 hours a day, that is 5.4 TB a day. To upload that much, you need about 500 Mbps of upload speed, all day and all night. Mobile data cannot carry this. Never upload over mobile data.

There are only two ways to upload. The first way is the site's own wireless internet. The phones stay at the site and upload there. The site's internet is tested on launch day. Most sites will not pass. The second way is a hub. We have three hubs on fiber: the central hub downtown, one hub in East Cairo, and one hub in West Cairo. Every night, a runner takes the site's phones to the nearest hub. Each hub is big enough for a full day. So one problem with a landlord, or one cut fiber line, cannot stop the company.

A location is not a hub until it passes the test. The test is 20 phones uploading for 8 hours at a steady 300 Mbps or better. Coworking spaces say they have "high speed" internet. That speed is shared with other people, and the upload speed is lower than the download speed. Measure the speed yourself. Do not believe what they tell you.

breaks.do: Send the runs to the next hub. Sites that upload on their own wireless internet are not affected. The backlog rule allows one day. Open a ticket with the ISP right away.

breaks.what: A vehicle is stolen or crashes
breaks.do: Use MDM to find the phones. Use lost mode to lock them. If we do not get them back, wipe them. File a police report the same day. File an insurance claim. Update the registry. Replace the phones from the 10% spare pool.

Show the letter, the commercial register, and the phone list. Call Moharam. Never argue. Never hide the number of phones. If the police keep the phones, Mano brings a lawyer and writes down what happened, the same day.
Check the storage every time a phone is docked. Swap a full phone for a spare, and flush the full phone first. A full phone is the Portfolio Manager's problem, and it must be fixed tonight.

questions.q: Why not upload over mobile data?
questions.a: Because the carrier decides how much data it will carry. At our volume, the carrier says no. Fiber is the only path that can grow with us.

questions.q: Why three hubs and not one big one?
questions.a: One hub means one landlord, one line, and one road. A second hub costs less than one lost day in a 25,000-hour month. It is also closer to the sites on that side of the city.

questions.q: A site will not let the phones leave overnight. What do we do?
questions.a: Then the site's wireless internet must pass the test on launch day. If it cannot, tell Moharam before launch. A phone never stays full overnight.

questions.q: Who pays for a site's internet upgrade?
questions.a: Usually we pay. It is usually cheap. We write it into the site agreement, so nobody argues about it later.

pipeline.hubTest: 20 phones uploading for 8 hours at 300 Mbps or better
pipeline.rule: Never keep more than a day of footage overnight.

paths.name: On-site wireless internet
paths.text: The phones stay at the site and upload there, every night. The site's wireless internet is tested on launch day: the site's phones must upload a full day of footage overnight. Most sites will not pass.

paths.name: Fiber at a hub
paths.text: Every other site is a hub site. Every night, a runner takes all of the site's phones to the nearest hub in one trip, in the provided bag. The person who hands over the phones signs, and the person who receives them signs.

hubs.name: Central hub
hubs.serves: Sites in the center of the city

transport.text: All of a site's phones go to the hub in one trip, in the provided bag. Nothing is written on the outside of the bag.
A printed phone list goes in the bag: the device numbers, the count, the site, the time out, and the runner's name. Both sides sign it at every handover.
Every runner carries the company letter in Arabic, printed on letterhead, a copy of the commercial register, the device list, and two phone numbers that someone will answer.
The person who hands over the phones signs, and the person who receives them signs, at pickup and at drop. MDM location tracking is on for every phone while it travels.
Runners never stop on the way.

en.title: To whom it may concern
body: {company}, commercial register number {register}, confirms that the person carrying this letter, {runner}, is transporting {devices} mobile phones and their accessories. The phones belong to the company. This person is moving them between the company's work sites and the company's upload facility, as part of the company's video data collection work.
The devices are company property. They are listed on the attached phone list. They are being carried on the company's instructions.
To confirm this at any hour, call {contact1} or {contact2}.

ar.title: إلى من يهمه الأمر
body: تؤكد شركة {company}، سجل تجاري رقم {register}، أن حامل هذا الخطاب، السيد/ {runner}، يقوم بنقل عدد {devices} هاتف محمول وملحقاتها، وهي مملوكة للشركة، بين مواقع عمل الشركة ومقر رفع البيانات الخاص بها، في إطار عمل الشركة في جمع بيانات الفيديو.
الأجهزة ملك للشركة، ومدرجة في البيان المرفق، ويتم نقلها بتعليمات من الشركة.
للتأكد في أي وقت، يرجى الاتصال على {contact1} أو {contact2}.
